extracted_factors.Label: Market Demand for Agricultural Commodities
extracted_factors.Description: The strong influence of market demand for agricultural commodities on deforestation, suggesting that higher prices can lead to increased deforestation as land is converted to meet demand.

extracted_factors.Label: Biophysical Characteristics
extracted_factors.Description: Exogenous factors such as slope, elevation, and soil suitability influence the economic activity land can support, affecting deforestation rates.

extracted_factors.Label: Proximity to Infrastructure
extracted_factors.Description: Proximity to roads and urban areas is consistently associated with higher deforestation due to reduced transportation costs and increased accessibility.

extracted_factors.Label: Protected Areas
extracted_factors.Description: Protected areas are consistently associated with lower deforestation, although their effectiveness varies with geographical and legal protection status.

extracted_pain_points.description: Land users often prefer the private benefits of alternative land uses over the public benefits of forests, leading to deforestation above the social optimum.
The challenge of effectively enforcing forest laws and regulations to prevent illegal deforestation activities.
Inconsistencies in policies like PES and land tenure security in effectively reducing deforestation.
